sections.h2: What should a seller know about Alabama before looking at a city or county guide?
sections.html:
Alabama is a Deep South state of about 5.16 million people, with a mountainous north, a coastal plain across most of the rest, and a short Gulf shoreline in the south. Where a house sits changes the weather it faces, the local offices a seller deals with and the pace of the market around it, while the state sets the rules for deeds, taxes and landlord disputes.

Alabama was admitted to the Union on December 14, 1819 as the 22nd state. Montgomery is the capital, Huntsville is the largest city by population and area, and Jefferson is the largest county. Greater Birmingham is the largest metro area and the state's economic center.

sections.h2: How is Alabama laid out, and why does it matter for a house sale?
sections.html:
About three fifths of the land area lies in the Gulf Coastal Plain, a gentle plain that slopes toward the Mississippi River and the Gulf of Mexico. North Alabama is mostly mountainous, and the Tennessee River cuts a large valley through it.

The land differs a lot from north to south. Forest covers about 67 percent of the state's land. Along the coast, Baldwin County is the largest county in the state by both land and water area, and it is described as suburban.

  • North Alabama: the Tennessee Valley, Appalachian Plateau and Ridge and Valley areas.
  • Central Alabama: Piedmont, Canebrake and the Black Belt, a band named for its dark, productive soil.
  • South Alabama: the Gulf Coastal Plain, Mobile Bay and the beaches on the Gulf of Mexico.

Mobile, founded by French colonists in 1702, is the oldest city in the state. Montgomery is the third most populous settlement.

sections.h2: What does the Alabama economy look like for homeowners?
sections.html:
It is diversified. Wikipedia lists automotive, finance, tourism, manufacturing, aerospace, mineral extraction, healthcare, education, retail and technology as the base of the 21st century economy.

Huntsville's aerospace cluster traces back to 1960, when NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center was established there and helped start a local aerospace industry.

The same source notes that Alabama typically ranks low on health outcomes, educational attainment and median household income.

sections.h2: What weather risks should Alabama sellers plan around?
sections.html:
Alabama has a humid subtropical climate, with an average annual temperature of 64 degrees Fahrenheit. The south runs warmer because of the Gulf, and the north runs cooler in the Appalachian foothills.

Two events show the scale of storm damage the state has seen:

  • Hurricane Ivan struck in 2004 as a Category 3 storm at landfall and caused more than $18 billion of damage.
  • A super outbreak of 62 tornadoes hit the state in April 2011 and killed 238 people, and a large tornado crossed downtown Cullman on April 27 of that year.

Alabama also ranks with Oklahoma and Iowa for the most confirmed F5 and EF5 tornadoes of any state from 1950 through June 2013. An owner with a storm-damaged house can sell it as it stands to a cash buyer.

sections.h2: Who records a deed in Alabama and what tax is due?
sections.html:
The judge of probate in the county where the property sits receives the deed, collects the tax and the recording fee, and records the instrument. Section 40-22-1 of the Alabama Code says a deed is not received for record until the privilege or license tax is paid.

The rate is 50 cents for each $500 of value conveyed, or part of $500, reduced by any mortgage on which the mortgage tax has already been paid. The state keeps two thirds of the tax and the county keeps one third.

  • The deed must come with proof of the actual purchase price, or of actual value if the property has not been sold.
  • A form developed by the Department of Revenue lets the person attest to the price without further documents.
  • A deed that covers land in two or more counties goes to the Department of Revenue, which fixes the value in each county.
  • Deliberately withholding requested proof or giving false proof carries a penalty of $100 or 25 percent of the tax, whichever is greater.

The probate judge's office is therefore the first stop for any closing, whether the property is in Birmingham, Mobile or a small county seat.

sections.h2: How does property tax work across Alabama?
sections.html:
Property tax follows one statewide calendar. The Alabama Department of Revenue lists the schedule as taxes due October 1 and delinquent January 1.

Unpaid taxes then move on a set path. The list is turned over to the probate court in February, the probate court meets in March, delinquent parcels are advertised for sale in April, and the tax sale takes place in May.

Sellers who inherit or buy late in the year should confirm with the county that the October bill has been paid, since a parcel that sits past January 1 enters that process. Our separate county and city property tax guides cover local offices and appeal steps.

sections.h2: Does Alabama have an estate tax?
sections.html:
No filing is required for estates of people who died after December 31, 2004. The Alabama Department of Revenue explains that the state's requirement was based on the federal estate tax credit, which federal legislation in 2001 phased out.

Heirs selling an inherited house still deal with the probate court, the deed recording tax and, in some cases, a fiduciary income tax return for the estate. Section 40-15-13 of the Alabama Code lets a personal representative record an affidavit that the estate is not taxable.

sections.h2: What are the basic eviction rules for a rented house in Alabama?
sections.html:
A landlord must give written notice first, and the court case follows. Under Section 35-9A-421, nonpayment and most breaches carry a notice with termination not less than seven business days after receipt, and a month-to-month tenancy needs 30 days under Section 35-9A-441.

Eviction cases are heard in district or circuit court in the county of the property, with scheduling precedence, and an appeal from a district court judgment must be filed within seven days. Our state pages on eviction notices and the eviction process walk through each step.

These rules apply statewide, so a landlord in Huntsville and a landlord in Dothan follow the same Act, though the courthouse and its clerk differ.

sections.h2: How do Alabama city and county differences affect a sale?
sections.html:
The state sets the rules, but a seller works with the local probate office, the county tax office and the city for permits, so details vary. Alabama's 461 municipalities hold 60.4 percent of the population on 9.6 percent of the land, so a good share of homes sit outside any city.

A seller unsure whether a house is inside a city can ask the county probate or revenue office.

Browse the city and county guides on this page for local specifics. If you want to skip repairs, showings and delays, tell us the address and we will talk through your options.

faqs.q: What is the largest city in Alabama?
faqs.a: Huntsville is the largest city by population and area, according to Wikipedia's Alabama article. Montgomery is the capital and Birmingham anchors the largest metro area.

faqs.q: When are Alabama property taxes due?
faqs.a: The Alabama Department of Revenue timetable shows taxes due October 1 and delinquent January 1, with the probate court receiving the list in February and a tax sale in May.

faqs.q: Who records a deed in Alabama?
faqs.a: The judge of probate in the county where the property is located records the deed after the recordation tax and fee are paid under Section 40-22-1.

faqs.q: How much is the Alabama deed tax?
faqs.a: Fifty cents for each $500 of value conveyed or fraction of $500, less value covered by mortgages that already paid mortgage tax.

faqs.q: Does Alabama charge an estate tax?
faqs.a: No filing is required for deaths after December 31, 2004, according to the Alabama Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: How much notice does an Alabama landlord give for unpaid rent?
faqs.a: Written notice that ends the lease not less than seven business days after receipt if the rent and late fees stay unpaid, under Section 35-9A-421(b).
